newsitem.title: FRANCE: France condemns West Bank shooting, urges calm.
newsitem.headline: France condemns West Bank shooting, urges calm.

text.p: France condemned the West Bank killing of a 12-year-old Israeli boy and his mother on Wednesday and called for calm to prevent a new flare-up of violence between Israelis and Palestinians.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman described the killing of the Jewish settlers as "odious" and said the culprits must be punished.
"The French government hopes that these murders, occurring in a charged atmosphere, will not trigger fresh violence," he said.
"Everything must be done to preserve calm...and break the current deadlock in the peace process," he said.
Five more Israelis were wounded in the West Bank drive-by shooting by Arab gunmen near the Palestinian-ruled town of Ramallah, Israeli security sources said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in charge of self-rule enclaves "that Israel would not let the incident pass quietly".

The killing prompted demands from Israeli settlers that the army initiate "hot pursuit" searches in the self-rule enclave. The issue of "hot pursuit" has snagged PLO-Israeli talks on an Israeli handover of most of the West Bank town of Hebron.
